track.name: product
track.label: Product & Strategy
track.summary: Learn how product managers uncover real customer problems, prioritize and roadmap ruthlessly, set product strategy, and partner with engineering and design to ship outcomes that move the metrics that matter.

phases.title: What Product Managers Actually Do
phases.description: What the PM role actually covers day to day, and how it differs from product owner and project manager roles.

phases.title: Product Discovery
phases.description: Talk to real customers, validate problems before solutions, and build the habit of continuous discovery.

phases.title: Prioritization & Roadmapping
phases.description: Turn a long list of ideas into a defensible priority order and a roadmap stakeholders can trust.

phases.title: Product Strategy
phases.description: Set a product vision, position against competitors, and connect day-to-day work to a coherent strategy.

phases.title: Working with Engineering & Design
phases.description: Write specs engineers can build from, speak the language of agile delivery, and collaborate as a true product trio.

phases.title: Product Metrics & Experimentation
phases.description: Pick metrics that actually reflect customer value, and use experiments instead of opinions to settle debates.

topics.title: What Product Managers Actually Do
topics.description: What the product manager role covers, and why it's centered on solving customer problems rather than managing a backlog.

topics.title: PM vs. Product Owner vs. Project Manager
topics.description: How these three commonly-confused titles differ in scope, focus, and day-to-day responsibilities.

topics.title: Empowered Product Teams vs. Feature Teams
topics.description: The difference between teams handed a list of features to build and teams handed problems to solve.

topics.title: Customer Interviews & Problem Discovery
topics.description: How to talk to customers in a way that surfaces real problems instead of confirming what you already believed.

topics.title: Continuous Discovery Habits
topics.description: Building a weekly cadence of small customer touchpoints instead of one big research phase before launch.

topics.title: Validating Problems Before Solutions
topics.description: Using lightweight opportunity assessments to decide whether a problem is worth solving before committing engineering time.

topics.title: RICE & Prioritization Frameworks
topics.description: Scoring competing ideas on reach, impact, confidence, and effort instead of prioritizing by opinion or seniority.

topics.title: Opportunity Solution Trees
topics.description: Mapping opportunities and solutions visually so a team can see and debate its options instead of jumping to one idea.

topics.title: Outcome-Based Roadmapping
topics.description: Building roadmaps around outcomes and time horizons instead of a fixed list of features and dates.

topics.title: Product Vision & Strategy Fundamentals
topics.description: The difference between a multi-year vision, a strategy, and the tactics that execute it.

topics.title: Competitive Positioning & Market Analysis
topics.description: Framing a product against competitive alternatives so the right customers immediately understand its value.

topics.title: Strategy Frameworks in Practice
topics.description: Applying a diagnosis-guiding policy-actions structure to tell a good strategy from a list of goals dressed up as one.

topics.title: Writing PRDs & Specs
topics.description: Writing a requirements document that aligns a team around the problem and success criteria, not just a feature list.

topics.title: Agile & Scrum Basics for PMs
topics.description: The ceremonies, roles, and vocabulary of Scrum a PM needs to work effectively with an agile engineering team.

topics.title: Cross-Functional Collaboration
topics.description: Working as a true trio with design and engineering so decisions get made together, not handed off in sequence.

topics.title: North Star Metrics & Product Metrics
topics.description: Choosing a single metric that captures customer value, and the input metrics that actually move it.

topics.title: A/B Testing Fundamentals for PMs
topics.description: The basics of running a valid experiment so a launch decision rests on evidence instead of the loudest opinion in the room.

resources.title: Product Management: An Introduction
resources.note: Cagan and Bob Baxley on why the heart of the PM job is product creation, not project coordination.

resources.title: What is product management
resources.note: A practitioner's plain-language explainer of what the role actually involves, from a widely-read PM newsletter.

resources.title: Product Manager vs. Product Owner
resources.note: Cagan's take on why he avoids the 'product owner' title and how it gets conflated with product manager.

resources.title: What's the difference between a product owner vs. a product manager?
resources.note: A side-by-side comparison that also places the project manager title in context.

resources.title: Article: Product vs Feature Teams
resources.note: The original, widely-cited framing of empowered product teams versus mercenary feature teams.

resources.title: Product vs. Project Teams
resources.note: A companion piece contrasting product teams with project-oriented teams organized around delivery dates.

resources.title: Product Discovery
resources.note: Walks through where customer interviews fit inside SVPG's overall discovery process.

resources.title: Teresa Torres on how to interview customers
resources.note: A detailed interview with Teresa Torres on avoiding common customer-interview mistakes.

resources.title: Continuous Discovery Habits by Teresa Torres
resources.note: A concise summary of the five habits Torres argues separate continuous discovery teams from the rest.

resources.title: Everyone Can Do Continuous Discovery—Even You! Here's How
resources.note: Torres's own site on getting a weekly customer-touchpoint habit started, even without dedicated research support.

resources.title: Assessing Product Opportunities
resources.note: A lightweight framework for scoping an opportunity before investing real discovery time in it.

resources.title: The Opportunity Backlog
resources.note: How to maintain a prioritized backlog of opportunities rather than jumping straight to a features backlog.

resources.title: RICE Prioritization Framework for Product Managers
resources.note: Written by the Intercom team that originally developed RICE, with the reasoning behind each factor.

resources.title: How to Use the RICE Framework for Better Prioritization
resources.note: A worked example that shows how to score and compare several ideas with RICE.

resources.title: Opportunity Solution Tree: Definition and Overview
resources.note: The clearest short definition of the tool, straight from the person who created it.

resources.title: Opportunity Solution Trees: Visualize Your Discovery to Stay Aligned and Drive Outcomes
resources.note: A deeper walkthrough of building and using a tree to connect discovery findings to prioritized bets.

resources.title: Outcome-Based Roadmaps: Mapping Impact, Not Features
resources.note: Explains how an outcome-based roadmap differs from a feature-and-date roadmap, with an example structure.

resources.title: The Alternative to Roadmaps
resources.note: Cagan's original, influential case for replacing feature roadmaps with problems and business objectives.

resources.title: Vision vs. Strategy
resources.note: Draws a clear line between the multi-year vision and the strategy used to get there.

resources.title: Product Design and Development
resources.note: A full MIT Sloan course on integrating marketing, design, and engineering when developing a new product.

resources.title: A Product Positioning Exercise
resources.note: A hands-on positioning exercise from the author of Obviously Awesome, posted free on her own site.

resources.title: Product Positioning Guide: Frameworks & Strategy
resources.note: A broader survey of positioning frameworks useful for comparing approaches beyond one single model.

resources.title: Richard Rumelt, Good Strategy Bad Strategy
resources.note: A thorough free summary of Rumelt's diagnosis-guiding policy-coherent actions 'kernel' and the hallmarks of bad strategy.

resources.title: Product Strategy in an Agile World
resources.note: Applies strategy thinking to the reality of iterative, agile product delivery.

resources.title: What is a Product Requirements Document (PRD)?
resources.note: A practical overview of what a PRD should contain and who it's written for.

resources.title: Lenny's Product Requirements template
resources.note: A free, ready-to-use PRD template built around crystallizing the problem before jumping to a solution.

resources.title: What is Scrum? Guide to the Agile Framework
resources.note: The standard reference for Scrum's ceremonies, artifacts, and roles that a PM will work inside of.

resources.title: Product Manager: Role & Best Practices for Beginners
resources.note: Ties the PM role specifically to how it functions inside an agile delivery cadence.

resources.title: Coaching - Collaboration
resources.note: Cagan's case that real collaboration with design and engineering, not hand-offs, is the core PM skill.

resources.title: Product Management vs. Engineering
resources.note: Explains why great products come from combining a real customer need with what engineering can newly make possible.

resources.title: Every Product Needs a North Star Metric: Here's How to Find Yours
resources.note: A practical walkthrough for choosing a single metric that reflects the value customers get from a product.

resources.title: The Role of Analytics
resources.note: Cagan on why comfort with data and analytics became a baseline expectation for product leaders.

resources.title: What are A/B tests: A guide for product managers
resources.note: Covers why experiments are necessary and the common statistical pitfalls PMs run into when reading results.

resources.title: AARRR: Come Aboard the Pirate Metrics Framework
resources.note: Introduces the acquisition/activation/retention/referral/revenue funnel PMs often test against.
